done_when: A follow-up that names a period the app reads itself (a month with or without a year, a year, a quarter with or without a year, or last, previous or this month, quarter or year) answers for that period whatever window the model emits; fiscal and other wording (FY, YTD, next month, previous week) keeps the model's window and the period control; a question naming no period still inherits or aggregates as before, and an amount is never read as a year; changing an answer's period still re-runs on the chosen period

findings.body: The Done-when remains unmet for accepted period and amount wording. The new parser checks for a bare year before extracting a named month, while the existing parser only accepts a directly adjacent `month year` form (`backend/src/chat/timeWindowParse.ts:92`). Consequently, common month-with-year forms such as “July of 2025” or “July, 2025” resolve to the whole of 2025. The special May pattern also misses an unambiguous bare follow-up such as “May?” or “Show May”, causing the previous/model window to win. Finally, the amount exclusions are prefix heuristics: phrases such as “Show Actual totaling 2025” still pass through `calendarYear` and become calendar-year queries, contrary to the requirement that an amount is never interpreted as a year.
findings.title: Not done: A follow-up that names a period answers for that period whatever window the model emits; a question naming no period still inhe

findings.body: The added regression scenarios still invoke `ChatService.ask` through `makeFixture`, whose model, executor, warehouse, audit, and selection resolver are fakes. The frontend period-control tests likewise mock the Ask API, and the repository has no Playwright configuration, browser specifications, or browser test command. Therefore named-period follow-ups, no-period inheritance/aggregation, and changing an answer's period remain unproven through the required browser, running API, real database, prior-turn transport, and period control. The successful close command only ran hermetic unit/component tests and does not close this required user-flow test gap.
findings.title: Not done: end-to-end Ask coverage for period selection and reruns

findings.body: This test directly asserts the private period-word classification, and it is the only reason `hasTimePeriodWords` is exported; production only needs the function inside `chat.service.ts`. Adjacent `ChatService.ask` tests already exercise the observable inheritance and aggregation behavior. Keeping this predicate-only test creates a test-only production API and would fail under behavior-preserving parser refactoring. Remove the export and this direct test, retaining coverage at the service boundary.
findings.title: Simpler: remove the exported detector test → cover period detection through ChatService.ask

why: An Ask question that names a period, such as July 2026, answers for that period even as a follow-up in the same thread; the model's own window and the previous answer's window used to win
